extraction.name: PIQA
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning formulated as a multiple-choice question answering task. It contains over 16,000 training QA pairs where a model must choose the most appropriate solution to a physical goal.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk; Rowan Zellers; Ronan Le Bras; Jianfeng Gao; Yejin Choi
extraction.citeAs: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi. PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by prompting crowdsourced annotators with links to instructables.com. Annotators were asked to articulate a physical goal, provide a valid solution, and write an invalid permutation (a trick) to serve as an incorrect solution.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The source data used to prompt annotators consisted of how-to instructions from instructables.com, drawn from six categories: costume, outside, craft, home, food, and workshop.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were prompted with links to instructables.com and asked to construct a physical goal, a valid solution, and an invalid trick solution. Data was collected via HITs, including a qualification HIT requiring >80% accuracy, and validated by other annotators.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Data was validated by other annotators for correctness, and examples with low agreement were removed from the data.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Reporting bias towards prototypical solutions and tools; stylistic annotation artifacts.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data, which often meant that correct examples requiring expert level knowledge of a domain (e.g., special woodworking terminology) were excluded as they do not fall under the umbrella of commonsense.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking progress in physical commonsense understanding; evaluating and studying physical commonsense understanding in natural language models.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data. The dataset was further cleaned of basic artifacts using the AFLite algorithm, which discards instances whose given feature representations are collectively highly indicative of the target label.
